external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders, and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: The shopper browses the storefront through the storefront API.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: The shopper submits orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes the orders database using a single application account.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable on the worker

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: receipt, including which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment to report that the order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone containing the only component exposed to the internet.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network containing the order service and orders database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because shoppers browse it and the card processor POSTs a webhook to it.
assumptions.basis: The description says shoppers browse the storefront through the API and that the card processor POSTs a webhook to it.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because callers reach it through gRPC.
assumptions.basis: The description explicitly identifies the storefront API's call to the order service as gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The shopper is in a separate tenant-controlled zone from the system.
assumptions.basis: The shopper is an external human actor who uses the storefront.

assumptions.assumption: The card processor is in a separate tenant-controlled zone.
assumptions.basis: The description explicitly says the card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API is in the internet-facing network zone.
assumptions.basis: The description says it is the only thing exposed to the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is in a separate tenant-controlled Cloud Storage zone.
assumptions.basis: The receipt archive is explicitly described as a Cloud Storage bucket, which is hosted by a cloud provider.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database has confidential data classification.
assumptions.basis: It contains shopper addresses and card-last-four, which are personal and payment-related data.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive has confidential data classification.
assumptions.basis: It contains receipts for completed orders, which are commercially and financially sensitive records.
